hypothesis: Keep the selected parent’s 256-thread CTA and matching 256-source tile, but stage only x, y, z, and mass in a 16-byte record. This reduces shared memory from 7,168 to 4,096 bytes while preserving source order and force arithmetic. The selected parent measured 0.00099616 s; compact tiles measured 0.00089008 s at 128 threads, 0.00092808 s at 160, and 0.00092263 s at 192. Since those results vary with tile size, this experiment tests compact staging at a fixed 256-thread configuration; no speedup is assumed. The catalog reports eight distinct programs and no repeats.
notes: The candidate uses 4,096 bytes of shared memory, below the selected parent’s successfully measured 7,168-byte allocation. All threads still reach both CTA barriers; source-tail loads, target reads, and output writes remain bounds-guarded. Correctness and performance are left to the official controller protocol.
